headline: Infleqtion, Honeywell Aerospace and UC Santa Barbara built a chip-sized prototype part that keeps lasers stable, a step toward handheld quantum sensors.
score_reason: Prototype announced by the companies, with no performance numbers or deployment dates.
importance_line: Makers of quantum sensors and clocks could get smaller parts, but this is a prototype described only in a company release, with no performance figures.
source: Infleqtion (press release), as carried by The Quantum Insider
summary: The Quantum Insider carries an Infleqtion press release saying the quantum technology company, Honeywell Aerospace and UC Santa Barbara built a prototype optical cavity, a component that keeps lasers stable, on a silicon chip instead of a large tabletop device. The partners say the design can be made in existing commercial chip factories and could lead to handheld sensors and precision timing, but the release gives no performance figures.
notes: HPCwire link (pool url) blocked; same press release read at The Quantum Insider. Company claims.
